name: pending-approval-expiry-transition-table
description: When introducing a new terminal failure reason: (1) add the enum variant, (2) EXTEND can_transition_to in fabro-types status.rs for every source status that can reach it, (3) update the contract test that pins per-reason transition expectations, (4) align the OpenAPI FailureReason enum (it had drifted: deadlock/soft_stop were missing). Symptom of a missed arm: append_event rejects with 'invalid status transition'.

content: Terminal workflow nodes (shape Msquare / exit) never dispatch a Handler: fabro-core executor.rs short-circuits them via on_terminal_reached. Test capture points must live on non-terminal nodes (e.g. wait/insulator with duration=1ms).

name: run-event-variant-touchpoints
description: Adding a run-event variant (fabro-94e8 pull_request.closed): seven touchpoints — fabro-types misc.rs Props + run_event/mod.rs EventBody variant/name/round-trip test, fabro-workflow event/events.rs variant+trace, names.rs, convert.rs, fabro-store run_state.rs reducer arm; EventBody is serde(tag=event,content=properties) so Unknown fallback makes it wire-compatible without migrations.

name: lifecycle-two-reducer-equivalence-via-shared-table
description: Proving server live fold and store RunProjectionReducer agree is done transitively (fabro-3fe4): one pure table fabro_types::apply_lifecycle_event consumed by BOTH, plus two thin equivalence tests (xorshift property test durable-reducer-vs-table in run_state.rs::lifecycle_equivalence, and live_lifecycle_status-vs-table step test in fabro-server server/tests.rs). Live-only guards (RunRunnable ingestion suppression) are documented deviations in the step test, not table arms. Historic pre-table stream shapes (Submitted->Starting jumps, fast-forwarded RunFailed) live in fabro_types::historic_skipped_statuses so the shim has one owner and the table stays strict.

checkpoint.completed run event exceeds MAX_RUN_EVENT_BODY_BYTES (3MB) on big merge-upstream runs: worker loses canonical run store (HTTP 413) AFTER the merge commit exists, run is marked failed(workflow_error), conductor pass soft-stops, and the merge work is stranded in the sandbox (fabro/run/* pushes rejected by GitHub branch protection, nothing persisted remotely). Observed 2026-09-11 on runs 01M27V69 and 01M2837. Salvage: docker start the stopped run container, docker cp .git out, fetch into host repo, push under salvage/<name> (fabro/run/* blocked, salvage/* allowed).
resolution: Unresolved: needs code fix — bound checkpoint event payload size (blob-store large data like tool outputs already do via MAX_SERIALIZED_TOOL_OUTPUT_BYTES) or raise MAX_RUN_EVENT_BODY_BYTES; independently allow-list fabro/run/* pushes so finished work is persisted before sandbox teardown. Interim manual salvage procedure documented in description.

name: retry-continuation-seam
description: Retry-as-continuation seam (fabro-183f): the executor's attempt context crosses the handler boundary as fabro_core::handler::AttemptInfo { attempt, prior_failure } — NodeHandler::execute and workflow Handler::execute take it as a last param; only AgentHandler consumes it (others take _attempt). PebbleBackend parks a retryably-failed conversation via export_for_reuse under the thread key (or the stage-id key when threadless; stage ordinals are stable across attempts via StageExecutionTracker::ensure) and sends continuation_message() instead of re-posting the prompt; a resumed execution learns it supersedes a prior one from the lifecycle-seeded internal.stage_resumed_from context key (transient, cleared at node boundaries). httpmock note: mocks match first-created-first, so overlapping matchers need mutually exclusive body_includes/body_excludes.
